A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same InfiniPot-V work. Text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-H are readable and can be matched across pagination and numbering changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original video-understanding evaluations, TaR/VaN ablations, qualitative case studies, and memory/latency measurements in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds evaluations on OVO-Bench and StreamingBench and deployment measurements on NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithms 1-2 retain the same continual compression procedure, TaR similarity scoring, VaN scoring with adaptive pooling, and combined token selection. The added evaluations do not introduce a method component.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluated coverage of OVO-Bench and StreamingBench to the retained offline benchmarks and RVS-Ego/Movie. These extend streaming evaluation to multiple-choice tasks covering backward tracing, real-time perception, and forward active responding, substantially broadening the tested streaming capabilities.

E2.justification: Corresponding original experiments retain their comparator sets, including SnapKV, InfiniPot, FastV, TTC/STC, ReKV, Uniform Select, and Full KV. New Tables 4 and 6 reuse Uniform Select and Full KV in added evaluations; no comparator is introduced or removed from a retained comparison.

E3.justification: v2 adds Qwen-2.5-VL-7B evaluations under a 4K memory budget and a separate Jetson deployment protocol using Qwen-2.5-VL-3B and ten-minute videos sampled at 0.2-1 FPS. The latter evaluates 100-600-second streams using memory, processing FPS, generation throughput, and energy measurements. These substantially extend evaluation settings without revising the retained protocols.

E4.justification: Section 4.4 adds a device-specific scaling analysis testing whether memory, throughput, and energy use remain manageable as streams lengthen, including an out-of-memory comparison. Existing component ablations, hyperparameter sweeps, multi-turn examples, and query-dependence analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions' Appendix E reports averages over five runs with three warmup iterations. Existing uncertainty displays are retained, and v2 adds no run-count, confidence-interval, or significance-test reporting for its new evaluations.

E6.justification: New Table 4 reports OVO-Avg scores of 53.6 versus 51.7 and StreamingBench scores of 76.4 versus 75.2 for InfiniPot-V versus Uniform Select. Table 6 adds Jetson results: at 500 seconds, memory is 10.7 versus 39.0 GB and throughput 9.1 versus 1.2 tokens/s; at 600 seconds, Full KV runs out of memory. These are newly reported settings. Retained results are unchanged apart from equivalent rounding in Table 2.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and reasoning for TaR, VaN, adaptive pooling, and attention-based cache selection are unchanged in Section 3 and Appendices A and D. No theorem, proof, or formal assumption is added or revised.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the central claims of training-free, query-agnostic compression with a fixed cache budget and strong streaming accuracy and efficiency. The conclusion is unchanged; the expanded experimental evidence supports the existing contribution rather than redefining it.

C2.justification: v2 adds task-specific interpretations of backward recall and real-time perception, and discusses compute-related energy savings and practical edge deployment. The positional-encoding caveat in Appendix B.4 and limitations concerning modalities and fixed budget allocation in Appendix H remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 supplies hardware, model, sampling-rate, duration, and memory-budget information for the added evaluations. Figure 1 also clarifies that its measurements use a single A100 80GB GPU. Existing appendix implementation details and hyperparameters remain unchanged; detailed energy-measurement procedures are not supplied.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations and brief descriptions for OVO-Bench and StreamingBench, increasing the reference list from 52 to 54 works. Appendix F and the positioning relative to prior compression methods are otherwise unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds Section 4.4 and localized benchmark descriptions and discussion, lightly rewrites the RVS comparison, standardizes ablation terminology, and updates the publication footer. The overall narrative, method exposition, and appendix structure remain stable.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 4 and 6, relocates and renumbers the original ablation table as Table 5, and makes small Figure 2 styling and table/caption formatting adjustments. Existing plots and appendix displays are retained without substantive visual restructuring.

improvement.justification: v1 motivates deployment on constrained edge devices but supports efficiency primarily with A100 measurements. v2 directly tests Jetson deployment, including successful 600-second inference where Full KV exhausts memory, addressing an important validation gap in the central application claim. The additional streaming tasks further strengthen empirical support. New comparisons and measurement documentation remain limited, especially for uncertainty and energy accounting, but the gain in practical validation is substantial.
